why_this_company.text: Nvidia dominated the week: results on Wednesday that beat forecasts, then a 23% weekly fall as investors worried about its CEO's exit and an export probe.

title: Nvidia: sales doubled, shares sank
hook: Record results, then a 23% fall in a week. What is the market actually betting on?
what_it_does: Designs the chips (GPUs) that train and run AI models, plus chips for gaming PCs and cars.
Its biggest customers are tech giants and cloud firms building huge AI data centres.
Its CUDA software is a moat: code written for Nvidia chips is hard to move elsewhere.
It doesn't own factories. Partners such as TSMC manufacture the chips it designs.

takeaways.price: Even after falling about 30% in a year, it has still left the S&P 500 far behind over five years.
takeaways.growth: Sales roughly doubled each year. The newest quarter ($115.8B, +103%) isn't in these figures yet.
takeaways.margins: About 56 cents of every sales dollar became profit last year: rare for a company selling hardware.
takeaways.health: Far more cash than debt, and it spent about $40B buying back its own shares last year.
takeaways.assumes: The price only bets on about 7% yearly cash-flow growth, far below its recent pace. The debate isn't growth today, it's how long it lasts.

bull.text: Sales more than doubled to $115.8B last quarter, and it expects about $130B next quarter.
It raised its forecast for sales growth in its next financial year to 75%, from 70%.
It keeps nearly 75 cents of each sales dollar as gross profit, a sign of real pricing power.

bear.text: Founder-CEO Jensen Huang resigned, and the board says it won't bring him back.
US authorities are examining whether its chips reached restricted buyers in China via a customer.
It has given about $118B of financial guarantees linked to customers' data-centre projects.
